# Rut.ts

> A modern TypeScript library for handling Chilean RUT (Rol Único Tributario) validation, formatting, cleaning, and generation with full type safety.

Rut.ts provides a comprehensive set of utilities for working with Chilean RUTs - the unique tax identification numbers used throughout Chile. The library supports validation (including strict mode for suspicious patterns), a branded `Rut` type narrowed by a type guard (`isValidRut`), a typed `InvalidRutError`, formatting (both standard and incremental for real-time input), masking for safe logging (`mask`), validity-aware comparison (`equals`), cleaning, decomposition, configurable random generation, and verifier digit calculation. It's fully typed, tree-shakeable, supports both ESM and CommonJS, and runs in Node.js (>= 20), the browser, Deno, and Bun. The RUT format follows the pattern `XX.XXX.XXX-Y` where the verifier digit is calculated using the Modulo 11 algorithm.

`validate()` and `isRutLike()` accept only three canonical shapes — compact (`123456785`), compact + hyphen (`12345678-5`), and canonical dotted (`12.345.678-5`), with optional surrounding whitespace (whatever JavaScript's `trim()` removes, Unicode spaces included), so one RUT can be written in several accepted ways: store or compare the `clean()` output, never the raw string. The body must be 7 or 8 digits (`1.000.000`–`99.999.999`): a shorter body is rejected even when its verifier is correct (`validate('999999-K')` is `false`, `calculateVerifier('999999')` throws), and historical RUNs below one million are deliberately out of scope. The dotted shape requires its verifier hyphen: `12.345.6785` (dots but no hyphen) is rejected, as is any non-canonical dot grouping (`12.345678-5`, `12345.678-5`). Leading-zero padding is also rejected by the acceptance predicates `validate()`/`isValidRut()`/`isRutLike()`: a canonical RUT carries no leading zeros, so `012.345.678-5` and `0012345678` are non-canonical and return `false`. For zero-padded/dirty input use the documented two-line recipe — `const rut = clean(raw, { throwOnError: false })` then `if (rut !== null && validate(rut)) accept(rut)` — which normalizes first and then proves the Modulo 11 verifier. `equals()` checks validity by default — `equals('12345678-9', '12345678-9')` is `false` (wrong verifier: not a RUT); pass `{ requireValid: false }` for the pure shape comparison. Validity is checked on the *normalized* value, so `equals('012345678-5', '12345678-5')` is `true` even though `validate('012345678-5')` is `false` — an intended asymmetry. Invalid input throws a typed `InvalidRutError` (catch it, or check `err.code === 'INVALID_RUT'`; both checks also hold for an error from another copy of the library, such as the CommonJS build loaded next to the ESM one). Input is capped at 64 characters as a security bound (not a format rule), and errors are a generic `Invalid RUT input` so Chilean ID values are never echoed into logs or traces. `clean()` and `decompose()` remain intentionally permissive for normalization (`clean('RUT: 12.345.678-5')` → `'123456785'`; it strips every non-`[0-9kK]` character wherever it sits) and must not be treated as validation — `clean` never checks the verifier digit. The API contract is frozen; release notes live in the CHANGELOG.

Key technical details:
- **Size**: ~3.89KB minified, ~1.80KB gzipped, as measured by [bundlejs](https://bundlejs.com/?q=rut.ts) — the same live source as the README badge (the shipped ESM dist file is slightly larger; a bundler re-minifies it away)
- **Zero dependencies**: Pure TypeScript implementation
- **Safe mode**: All throwing functions support `{ throwOnError: false }` to return `null` instead of throwing (defaults frozen until a hypothetical v6)
- **Strict validation**: `validate(rut, { strict: true })` additionally rejects repeated-digit placeholder RUTs (e.g. `11.111.111-1`)
- **Secure generation**: `generate()` uses Web Crypto (`crypto.getRandomValues`, guaranteed on Node >= 20) with unbiased rejection sampling; a `Math.random()` fallback is retained only as a safety net for exotic runtimes without Web Crypto
- **Dual package**: Native ESM with CommonJS fallback
- **Type definitions**: Full TypeScript support with exported types (including `EqualsOptions`)

## Core API Functions

- [validate()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/validate): Validate RUT format and verifier digit with optional strict mode to detect suspicious patterns
- [format()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/format): Format RUTs with dots and hyphens, supports incremental mode for real-time input (a trailing hyphen after a complete body is kept as "verifier pending" — `12345678-` → `12.345.678-` — and a `K` is always treated as the verifier, however short the input — `7612K` → `7.612-K`)
- [clean()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/clean): Remove formatting, special characters, and leading zeros from RUT strings
- [decompose()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/decompose): Split a RUT into its body (numeric part) and verifier digit components
- [calculateVerifier()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/calculate-verifier): Calculate the correct verifier digit for a given RUT body using Modulo 11
- [generate()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/generate): Generate valid random RUT numbers for testing and development
- [getBody()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/get-body): Extract only the body (numeric part) from a formatted or unformatted RUT
- [getVerifier()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/get-verifier): Extract only the verifier digit from a formatted or unformatted RUT
- [isRutLike()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/is-rut-like): Check if a string matches RUT format without full validation
- [isValidRut()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/is-valid-rut): Type guard that narrows a value to the branded `Rut` type when valid (supports strict mode)
- [mask()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/mask): Mask a RUT for safe logging/display, keeping only the leading group and verifier (`12.345.678-5` → `12.***.***-5`)
- [equals()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/documentation/features/equals): Answer "same RUT?" across shapes — normalizes both arguments and, by default, requires the shared value to pass Modulo 11 (`{ requireValid: false }` gives the pure shape comparison)
- [RUT_PATTERN](https://github.com/arrowsw/rut.ts/blob/canary/README.md): The accepted shapes as anchored, flagless, backslash-free regex strings (`any`, `compact`, `hyphen`, `dotted`) for JSON Schema / OpenAPI `pattern`, zod `regex` and database `CHECK` constraints. Shape only — it never proves the verifier digit, so pair it with `validate()`; prefer `hyphen`/`dotted` in API schemas because `any`/`compact` match any 9-digit number. `isRutLike(s) === new RegExp(RUT_PATTERN.any).test(s.trim())` for inputs up to 64 chars
- [InvalidRutError](https://github.com/arrowsw/rut.ts/blob/canary/README.md): Typed error (class with `code: 'INVALID_RUT'`) thrown by the safe helpers; catch it instead of matching the message text. Both `err instanceof InvalidRutError` and `err.code === 'INVALID_RUT'` also match an error thrown by another copy of the library in the same process (the ESM and CommonJS builds side by side, another installed version, another realm); `err.code` is the check that also works when the other copy is an older `rut.ts`
